name: mkldnn_convolution
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::mkldnn_convolution(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias, SymInt[] padding, SymInt[] stride, SymInt[] dilation, SymInt groups) -> Tensor. This definition is representative only and NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract, so overloads, keyword arguments, return identity, errors, aliasing and mutation must keep being defined by that pytest and must never be narrowed, deleted or rewritten to fit this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::mkldnn_convolution(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias, SymInt[] padding, SymInt[] stride, SymInt[] dilation, SymInt groups) -> Tensor ; aten::mkldnn_convolution.out(Tensor self, Tensor weight, Tensor? bias, SymInt[] padding, SymInt[] stride, SymInt[] dilation, SymInt groups, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: oneDNN (MKLDNN) CPU convolution over an N-dimensional input (tested at ranks 3 NCL, 4 NCHW and 5 NCDHW) with per-spatial-dim padding, stride, dilation and grouped/depthwise convolution; bias may be None (bias-absent form) and, for int8/uint8 inputs, the tests pass a float32 bias because integer bias descriptors are rejected natively. Operands may be dense CPU tensors or torch._mkldnn tensors, including channels-last, sliced, offset, transposed and strided memory layouts; the native kernel keeps the operand layout (the pytest states that a channels-last input yields a channels-last-strided output and contiguous operands yield a contiguous output), and the tests compare the candidate output stride against the reference output stride in addition to values, and assert res_out.layout == torch._mkldnn for torch._mkldnn operands, so layout must be asserted as well as values. The default overload returns a new tensor and does not mutate its inputs (the pytest verifies input and weight are unchanged); with dense CPU operands the result is dense, while with torch._mkldnn operands the result layout is torch._mkldnn. The .out overload is keyword-only (out=...), mutates and returns the same buffer object (return identity, not just equal contents) and resizes an empty or undersized buffer to the computed convolution shape; it requires the out dtype to equal the input dtype. Distinct overload-dependent effects are not expressed here and remain covered by pytest. Errors validated by the tests, not by this definition: rank-2 input, rank-1 or rank-6 shapes, input-channel/groups mismatch, groups <= 0, channels not divisible by groups, bias-size mismatch, zero stride, zero dilation, negative padding, kernel larger than input, dilation pushing the kernel out, integer bias dtypes, out dtype mismatch, and unsupported dtypes (float64, int16, int32, int64, bool, complex, fp8) which raise at the native dtype check. Backward support (test_mkldnn_convolution_backward) autograds through this forward for float32/float16/bfloat16 only.
